note.headline: Stocks bounce, but trend, fear and breadth still say stand aside

summary.thesis: SPY rose 1.62% and QQQ 2.69% on Nov 27, but both remain in downtrends below their 50- and 200-day averages. Fear is still 'elevated' and only 8% of stocks are above their 50-day averages.
summary.decision: Stand aside for both long-term buying and swing setups. The market gate stays active until QQQ closes above 682.74.
summary.act_at: A QQQ close above 682.74 (its 200-day average and the market gate) would end the tech downtrend. A QQQ close below 608.45 or SPY below 689.81 would set new 1-month lows, meaning the decline would be continuing.

note.happening: Stocks had a strong day on Nov 27. SPY closed at 728.32, up from 716.70 (+1.62%), and QQQ closed at 650.99, up from 633.93 (+2.69%). Over five days SPY is up 1.74% and QQQ up 0.92%. Over 20 days both are still down, SPY by 5.33% and QQQ by 9.0%. Both bounced off 1-month lows set on Nov 20 (SPY 689.81, QQQ 608.45). Both remain well under their Oct 29 1-month highs (SPY 769.36, QQQ 715.34) and their past-year highest closes on Oct 6 (SPY 779.09, QQQ 759.66). No news was recorded since the last note. The next scheduled event is the jobs report (Employment Situation) on Dec 4 at 08:30, which shapes rate expectations.
note.business: Trend: both indices are below their 50- and 200-day averages, which DATA classifies as a downtrend. SPY is close to its long-term line, 0.4% below its 200-day average of 730.98. QQQ is further away, 4.9% below its 200-day average of 682.74. Fear: the VIX was 26.8 on Nov 26, down from 28.29. That is still in the 'elevated' band (20–30) and at the 96th percentile of its last 252 readings, near the top of its one-year range of 13.47 to 35.89. This reading is stale: the Nov 27 VIX isn't stored yet, so today's rally is not reflected in it. Breadth: only 8% of stocks are above their 50-day averages, so very few stocks are in short-term uptrends. Read together, the bounce is real but narrow so far. Prices rose for a day, while the underlying trend, fear and participation readings still describe a market under stress. The recovery is not yet confirmed.

worth.text: No valuation is implied for the indices. The levels in this note are price-trend markers only.
worth.key_assumption: No valuation is implied. The levels are price-trend markers only.

bull: Both indices rallied on Nov 27 (SPY +1.62%, QQQ +2.69%) and are up over five days, holding above their Nov 20 1-month lows.
SPY is only 0.4% below its 200-day average of 730.98. A close above it would put the broad market's long-term trend back up.
The VIX eased from 28.29 to 26.8, and its five-day change is -1.64, so fear has stepped back from its recent level.
bear: Both SPY and QQQ remain below their 50- and 200-day averages, and DATA labels both trends 'downtrend'.
Breadth is 8%: very few stocks are in short-term uptrends, so the rally is not broad-based.
The VIX is still 'elevated' at the 96th percentile of its past 252 readings, and the latest stored value predates today's move.

note.headline: Tesla jumps 5.22% to 400.0, past its valuation top; still avoid

summary.thesis: Today's rally made a weakening business more expensive. At 400.0 Tesla trades just above the 399.81 top of its own 5-year price-to-sales range, while sales are flat and margins and cash flow are shrinking.
summary.decision: Long-term: avoid. Swing: wait, because the price sits inside a busy zone just under resistance at 408.62–420.34.
summary.act_at: Re-examine near 293.94 after the 2027-01-27 report; swing only on a close above 420.34

note.happening: Tesla rose 5.22% to 400.0. That lifts it out of the 380.15–389.95 zone and into the 393.63–404.4 band, just under resistance at 408.62–420.34 (8 touches). There is no news since the last note, and the next earnings report is on 2027-01-27.
note.business: Nothing new changed the business today. The move was price and sentiment only. The latest filing (2026-10-22) still shows the business weakening. Quarterly sales fell 0.17% from a year earlier, after growing 15.78% two quarters ago. Operating margin (profit from operations per dollar of sales) slipped to 3.35% from 4.74%. Free cash flow (cash left after spending on the business) over the last 12 months fell to 3.3B from 6.8B. The filings flag inventory up 15% while latest-quarter sales were up 0%. Unsold cars can lead to price cuts and thinner margins, so demand and margins are what is at risk. Each dollar invested now earns 5¢ a year, against 33¢ three years ago. The balance sheet is not at risk: net cash is 37.5B, liquidity is 45.4B and total debt is only 8.0B. Share dilution is small at 0.43% a year. The business grade is D.

worth.text: At 400.0 the market values Tesla at 1581.0B. That is 15.3 times sales and 440.1 times trailing earnings. The filings note that this price needs about 51% a year growth, against 3% a year delivered over 3 years. A discounted cash flow model (today's value of future cash) built on the current 3.3B of free cash flow gives only 20.17–45.0 per share, with a base of 24.93. Even at 30% starting growth it reaches just 45.37. The other method asks what investors have paid for each dollar of Tesla's sales in the past. It gives 203.8 to 293.94 to 399.81, and today's price sits at that top. The gap between the methods comes down to one assumption. The cash-flow model takes today's thin cash flow at face value. The history method assumes investors keep paying past multiples for Tesla's story. Weighing flat sales against a strong balance sheet, I put fair value in the low-to-middle part of the history range.
worth.key_assumption: With flat quarterly sales and operating margin down to 3.35%, the market will value Tesla in the low-to-middle part of its 5-year price-to-sales range, not at the 399.81 top it reached today.

bull: Net cash of 37.5B and liquidity of 45.4B give Tesla room to keep spending through a weak patch.
12-month sales still grew to 103.6B from 95.6B (8.3%), so the slowdown is recent, not long-running.
Today's close at 400.0 is above all three moving averages (20-day 381.98, 50-day 377.84, 200-day 381.0), and the 400 call is the busiest options strike with 14172 contracts open.
bear: At 440.1 times trailing earnings, the price needs about 51% a year growth, against 3% a year delivered over 3 years.
Operating margin fell to 3.35% from 4.74%, and 12-month free cash flow fell to 3.3B from 6.8B.
Inventory is up 15% while latest-quarter sales are up 0%, which can force price cuts and squeeze margins further.

levels.what: Today's close. It is just above the own-history top of 399.81 and far above the cash-flow base of 24.93, so value gives no support here.
Bottom of the lower support zone (363.85–368.77, 4 touches). A close below it would end the range and point lower.
Middle of the own-history price-to-sales range and the top of my fair-value range. Re-examine here only if the 2027-01-27 report shows operating margin back above 4.74%.

longterm.why: Sales, margins, cash flow and returns on investment are all weakening, and the price now sits at the top of its own valuation history. The business grade is D and the internal committee call is Reduce.

swing.why: The trend is a range with flat averages. The price sits just under resistance at 408.62–420.34 (8 touches), so the room above is small next to a typical daily swing (ATR, the average daily range) of 19.68. No trade until a close above 420.34, or until a pullback holds the 380.15–389.95 zone (9 touches).

decision.timing: No new long-term position before the 2027-01-27 report. Options price an 11.5% move by 2026-12-18 and a 20.2% move by 2027-02-19, which covers the report. Actual recent swings (75.4) have been bigger than what options imply (56.1). These options figures come from 2026-11-25, before today's jump.

change_mind: The 2027-01-27 report shows operating margin back above 4.74% and quarterly sales growth back toward the 15.78% of two quarters ago.
The price falls to 293.94, the middle of the own-history range, without further margin damage.
A daily close above 420.34 would clear resistance and support a swing entry. A close below 363.85 would confirm the range has broken lower.
note.what_changed: Unchanged: still avoid. The 5.22% jump to 400.0 pushed the price just past the 399.81 top of its own valuation history, which confirms that value offers no cushion at this price.
note.label: Research, not advice.

note.headline: NVIDIA closes 150.49 atop support as Huang-return and governance stories are reported

summary.thesis: NVIDIA is growing fast and makes a lot of cash, and the price already assumes about 19.1% starting cash-flow growth. That is cheap only if the 65.21% operating margin, the top of its 5-year range, holds.
summary.decision: Long-term hold, not add, because the margin and customer-payment risks are open. No swing trade while the downtrend holds.
summary.act_at: Buy at 117.15, trim near 226.93, wait on a close below 147.19

note.happening: NVIDIA closed at 150.49, up 0.8%. That sits just above the 147.19–150.41 support zone, the price area where buyers stepped in before. The trend is still down: the price is below its 20-day average of 169.32 and its 50-day average of 202.28, and both are falling. Today's news is commentary: CNBC and the FT reported on Jensen Huang's return and on an update to NVIDIA's code of conduct. Our data has no earnings date.
note.business: The numbers that drive the business are strong and improving. Last quarter's sales grew 105.85% from a year earlier, up from 73.21% two quarters ago. The operating margin, meaning the share of sales left as operating profit, rose to 65.21% from 58.09%. Free cash flow, the cash left after running and investing in the business, reached 127.0B, up from 72.0B. NVIDIA has more cash than debt, with net cash of 23.2B. Analysts have raised next year's earnings estimate (EPS) by 27.7% over 90 days. The filings show three real risks. The margin is at the top of its 5-year range (16–65%), and margins that high tend to fall back. Money customers owe but have not yet paid rose 127%, while sales rose 106%, both compared with a year earlier. That can mean sales were pulled forward or customers are stretched. Insiders also sold $946.6M of stock outside pre-set plans. Today's reported news on Huang's leadership and the code of conduct affects sentiment and governance only. Nothing in our data shows it changing demand, margins or cash. The shipment halt mentioned in the previous note's headline does not appear in today's news, so its effect on the business is still unknown. Demand and cash generation are not at risk based on the current numbers. The height of the margin and the quality of sales, given the slow customer payments, are at risk.

worth.text: At 150.49, the stock is valued at 18.9 times last year's earnings and 9.1 times next year's expected earnings. It trades at 12.0 times sales, below the peer median of 13.4 and in the 4.0th percentile of its own 5-year range. A discounted cash flow model (DCF) values a company by projecting its future cash and converting it to today's money. Our DCF gives 194.8 in the bear case, 226.93 in the base case and 270.18 in the bull case. Valuing the stock on its own past price-to-sales levels gives 217.35 to 411.04. Every method lands above today's price. Working backward, the price implies free cash flow growth starting at 19.1%. At 20% starting growth the model gives 155.88, and at 10% it gives 105.42. Most of the gap between the methods comes from the margin. If the operating margin falls to 48%, value drops to 117.15, and at 32% it drops to 78.42. So the stock looks cheap only if most of today's peak margin lasts.
worth.key_assumption: The operating margin stays near 65.21% instead of fading toward 48%, and free cash flow growth starts above the 19.1% the price implies.

bull: The stock trades at only 9.1 times next year's expected earnings, and analysts raised that earnings estimate by 27.7% over 90 days.
Free cash flow rose to 127.0B from 72.0B, and the company holds 23.2B more cash than debt.
Price-to-sales of 12.0 is below the peer median of 13.4 and in the 4.0th percentile of NVIDIA's own 5-year range.
bear: The 65.21% operating margin is at the top of its 5-year range. If it falls to 48%, the model value drops to 117.15, below today's 150.49.
Unpaid customer bills rose 127% while sales rose 106%, which can mean sales were pulled forward or customers are stretched.
The price is in a downtrend below its falling 50-day average of 202.28, and insiders sold $946.6M of stock outside pre-set plans.

levels.what: Bottom of the support zone the price sits on (147.19–150.41). A close below it moves the call to wait. The next support is 122.89–126.11.
Model value if the operating margin falls to 48%. Buy at 117.15, because that price already allows for a large margin fade.
Base-case cash-flow value. Trim near it, because at that price the peak margin and strong growth would be fully priced in.

longterm.why: The automated rule says 'Buy now' and the committee says 'Hold'. The price looks cheap only if the peak margin holds, and slow customer payments are unresolved. So the call is hold, not add.

swing.why: The chart shows lower highs and lower lows. A typical day moves 12.9 (the average true range, or ATR), which is wider than the gap down to 147.19, so any tight stop would likely be hit by normal moves. The next support below is 122.89–126.11. No trade until a close above 171.5, the top of the resistance zone the price has hit 5 times.

decision.timing: Our data has no earnings date, and the options market prices a 14.7% move by 2026-12-18 with no earnings in that window. So the timing depends on the price holding 147.19 or breaking 171.5, not on the calendar.

change_mind: A close below 147.19 moves the long-term call from hold to wait, with the next support at 122.89–126.11.
A next filing with the operating margin back below 58.09%, or unpaid customer bills still growing faster than the 106% sales growth, would end the case for holding near 150.49.
A close above 171.5, the top of the 5-touch resistance zone, would end the downtrend case and reopen a swing entry.
note.what_changed: Unchanged: still hold, because the price held its support zone and closed at 150.49, above the 147.19 floor, while the margin and receivables risks remain.
note.label: Research, not advice.

note.headline: AMD bounces 4.56% to 424.54, but price still sits far above fair value

summary.thesis: AMD is growing fast and getting more profitable, but at 424.54 the price assumes years of growth well beyond what any valuation method in the data supports.
summary.decision: Long-term: wait for a price near the top of the fair-value range. Swing: no trade while the downtrend holds.
summary.act_at: Long-term at 333.38 or lower; swing only after a close above 451.0

note.happening: AMD rose 4.56% to 424.54. That puts it inside the 424.03–451.0 zone and just below its 200-day average of 434.01, while the 20-day average of 482.13 is still falling and the trend reads as a downtrend. There is no news since the last note, and the next earnings report is on 2027-02-02.
note.business: The business itself is strong and improving. Sales over the last twelve months were 45.4B, up from 32.0B. Growth in the latest quarter was 44.68% versus a year earlier, faster than the 37.85% two quarters ago. Operating margin (profit from operations per dollar of sales) rose to 17.72% from 8.78%. Free cash flow (cash left after running and investing in the business) grew to 7.1B from 5.4B. The balance sheet is safe, with 8.7B of net cash (cash minus debt), so financing is not at risk. Analysts raised next-year EPS (earnings per share) estimates by 11.3% in 30 days, to 17.64. What is at risk is how long this lasts. The filings flag inventory up 57% against sales up 45%, which can lead to price cuts and lower margins. They also note that the 18% operating margin sits at the top of its 5-year range, and peaks like that usually fade. Competition in AI chips with larger rivals such as Nvidia (general knowledge) bears on that too. Today's bounce, the tech-sector downtrend and the elevated fear noted by the macro read change sentiment only. They do not change the business.

worth.text: Every valuation method lands below today's price. A discounted cash flow model values future free cash flow in today's money. It gives 147.69 in the bear case, 189.77 in the base case and 225.08 in the bull case. AMD's own price-to-sales history gives 179.24 to 333.38. The gap comes from the growth assumption. To justify the price, cash flow would have to start growing at about 53.1% a year. The model caps starting growth at 30%, and even 30% gives only 190.08. The multiples tell the same story. The price is 92.6 times trailing earnings and 52.5 times this year's estimate. It is 24.1 times next year's estimate, but only if EPS reaches 17.64. That would mean analysts' 118% next-year EPS growth comes true. Price-to-sales of 15.3 is above the peer median of 12.0 and at the 88th percentile of AMD's own 5-year range. Margins matter too: if operating margin fell to 13%, the value drops to 100.16.
worth.key_assumption: Starting cash-flow growth: the price implies about 53.1% a year against a 30% cap, so it holds up only if analysts' 118% next-year EPS growth comes true and keeps going.

bull: Growth is speeding up: latest-quarter sales growth of 44.68% beats the 37.85% of two quarters ago.
Profitability doubled: operating margin rose to 17.72% from 8.78%, and free cash flow grew to 7.1B from 5.4B.
Analysts are getting more upbeat: next-year EPS estimates rose 11.3% in 30 days to 17.64, which puts the forward multiple at 24.1.
bear: The price of 424.54 is above the whole fair-value range, whose top is 333.38.
Inventory is up 57% while sales are up 45%, a setup that can force price cuts and squeeze margins.
Valuation is stretched: price-to-sales of 15.3 is above the peer median of 12.0 and at the 88th percentile of AMD's own 5-year range.

levels.what: Today's close. It is above every valuation method, so it is not a buy price.
Bottom of the 392.08–403.38 support zone. A close below it points to the next zone at 347.34–358.64, which is still above fair value.
Top of the fair-value range, from AMD's own price-to-sales history. The value case for buying starts here.

longterm.why: The business is strong and improving, but the price needs far faster lasting growth than the data supports. Wait for 333.38 or lower, or for results that support much faster lasting growth.

swing.why: The trend is down: the 20-day average of 482.13 is falling and the price is below the 50-day average of 545.94. The average daily range (ATR) of 45.21 is wider than the 392.08–403.38 support zone, so a stop there would sit inside normal daily swings. No trade until a close above 451.0, the top of the 424.03–451.0 zone.

decision.timing: The 2027-02-02 report is over two months away. Options price an 18.7% move by 2026-12-18 and 30.2% by 2027-02-19. The largest put open interest (outstanding bearish contracts) is at the 350 strike, so mood alone could push the price through support before the report.

change_mind: A drop to 333.38 or lower, with the business intact, would turn the long-term call to buy.

A 2027-02-02 report showing quarterly growth above 44.68% and operating margin at or above 17.72%, with the next-year EPS estimate holding at 17.64 or higher, would support more of the implied 53.1% growth.
Inventory growth staying ahead of sales (57% versus 45% now), or operating margin falling back toward 13%, where value drops to 100.16, would move the call toward avoid.
note.what_changed: Unchanged: still wait, because today's 4.56% rise to 424.54 leaves the price even further above the 333.38 top of the fair-value range.
note.label: Research, not advice.

note.headline: Amazon rises 3.96% to 254.12; still waiting for 238.65 before buying

summary.thesis: Amazon's sales and operating margin are growing, but cash flow has turned sharply negative and growth is slowing, and at 254.12 the price sits above the 238.65 middle of its own value range.
summary.decision: Long-term: wait for 238.65. Swing: no trade while the price sits inside the 251.93–258.08 zone and below the 257.7 20-day average.

note.happening: Amazon closed at 254.12, up 3.96% on the day, and has recovered from the 244.43 of the last note. The price is now inside a 251.93–258.08 zone, just under its 20-day (257.7) and 50-day (255.17) averages, and the overall trend is still down. The only news of note is a reported CNBC story that Amazon and other sites are limiting AI shopping agents, and the next earnings report is on 2027-02-04.
note.business: Some things change the business itself. Yearly sales reached 797.5B, up from 691.3B, and the operating margin (profit from operations per dollar of sales) rose to 13.09% from 11.02%. But growth in the latest quarter slowed to 12.09% from a year earlier, down from 16.61% two quarters ago. Free cash flow (cash left after running the business and paying for investment) fell to -46.9B from 10.6B, so Amazon now spends more cash than it brings in. Debt of 180.9B is larger than cash of 55.8B, which leaves net debt of 66.7B. Liquidity of 114.2B means there is no near-term funding strain. The filings flag two more points: unpaid customer bills grew 61% while sales grew 12%, which can mean sales were pulled forward or customers are paying more slowly, and the 13% margin is at the top of its 5-year range of 2–13%. Other things change mainly sentiment. The reported AI-shopping-agent story is about competition for how shoppers find products. Amazon's choice to block these agents protects its own store for now (general knowledge), and nothing in the data shows an effect on sales yet. At risk: cash generation and how long the margin stays this high. Not at risk: liquidity and sales scale.

worth.text: There is no discounted-cash-flow value because free cash flow is negative. The only method left is Amazon's own price-to-sales history (the company's value divided by its yearly sales). That method gives 187.93 at the low end, 238.65 in the middle and 265.96 at the high end. At 254.12 the price is above the middle and below the top, and today's price-to-sales of 3.4 sits at the 60th percentile of its own 5-year range. On earnings, the stock trades at 20.6 times trailing earnings and 19.9 times this year's estimate, but at 23.8 times next year's. That is because next year's earnings estimate (10.67) is below this year's (12.8). The filings note that the price needs about 33% a year growth, against 13% a year delivered over 3 years. Against peers, Amazon looks cheap: 3.4 times sales versus a peer median of 6.5, and 0.58 on a growth-adjusted basis. The whole gap between the two views comes from one question: is Amazon priced against its own past or against those peers?
worth.key_assumption: Amazon's price-to-sales stays within its own 5-year range instead of moving toward the peer median of 6.5.

bull: Operating margin rose to 13.09% from 11.02%, so each dollar of sales now earns more operating profit.
At 3.4 times sales, Amazon trades well below the peer median of 6.5, and 0.58 on a growth-adjusted basis.
Analysts raised next year's earnings estimate by 1.4% over 30 days, to 10.67.
bear: Free cash flow swung to -46.9B from 10.6B, and net debt stands at 66.7B.
Unpaid customer bills rose 61% while quarterly sales rose 12%, which may mean sales were pulled forward.
Quarterly growth slowed to 12.09% from 16.61% two quarters ago, and the next-quarter earnings estimate was cut 2.6% in 30 days.

levels.what: The middle of the own-history value range. It sits inside the 233.59–238.97 support zone (3 touches). This is the main buy level.
The bottom of that support zone. A close below it means the zone failed, and the 187.93 low of the value range comes into view before any added buying.
The top of the own-history value range. No buying above it.

longterm.why: At 254.12 the price is further above the 238.65 middle of the value range than it was at the last note. Meanwhile the cash burn, the slowing growth, the D business grade and the 'Reduce' committee call are all unchanged.

swing.why: The price is in a downtrend, sits inside the 251.93–258.08 zone, is below the 257.7 20-day average, and has resistance just above at 259.49–265.34. Its typical daily move is 10.47, which leaves little room before the next barrier. No trade until either a close above 258.08 or a pullback that holds the 244.3–249.71 support zone (9 touches).

decision.timing: The 2027-02-04 report is the next real test: options expiring 2027-02-19 price in a move of about 16.3%, against 8.5% for 2026-12-18, so any buy before the report starts at 238.65 and no higher.

change_mind: The quarterly sales growth in the 2027-02-04 report returns above 16.61% and free cash flow moves back toward the prior 10.6B. That would support buying closer to the 265.96 top of the value range.
A close above 265.34, the top of the first resistance zone, would end the lower-highs pattern and allow a swing entry.
A close below 233.59 would break the support around the 238.65 buy level. The buy level would then move down toward the 187.93 low of the value range.
note.what_changed: Unchanged: still wait. The 3.96% rise to 254.12 moved the price further above the 238.65 buy level, and free cash flow is still negative at -46.9B.
note.label: Research, not advice.

note.headline: Microsoft edges up to 492.85 above support; hold and dip-buy swing plan unchanged

summary.thesis: Microsoft's sales and profit margins keep improving, but free cash flow is shrinking and the stock already prices in fast cash growth, so it is fairly valued against its own history and not cheap.
summary.decision: Long-term: hold, and add only at 474.82. Swing: keep yesterday's plan, buying a dip to 485.06 with a stop at 475.34 and a target of 503.99.
summary.act_at: Add at 474.82; swing buy at 485.06, stop 475.34, target 503.99

note.happening: The stock closed at 492.85, up 0.6%. That is just above its strongest support zone, 485.58–490.27, which has held 7 times, and below the falling 20-day average at 514.56. There is no new news since the last note, and the next earnings report is on 2027-01-27.
note.business: Three things describe the business itself: demand, margins and cash. Demand is strong.
